page.overview:
What is War of Wrath?

The War of Wrath, also called the Great Battle, was a clash of Elves, Men, Dwarves and Ainur against the forces of the fallen Vala Morgoth, marking both the end of the First Age and of Morgoth's rule in Middle-earth. It was the largest battle to ever occur in Arda. It resulted in the expulsion of Morgoth from Arda and the ruin of Thangorodrim, but the violence and tumult of the clashes between the forces of the Valar and of Morgoth shattered the northwestern portion of Middle-earth, Beleriand, causing it to sink beneath the ocean.

By the early sixth Years of the Sun of the First Age, Morgoth's dominion had become completely uncontested in Middle-earth. The efforts of Elves and Men to resist him had failed, and all of the great Elven kingdoms in exile had been overthrown. Morgoth was now master of nearly all of Beleriand, save for the havens in Arvernien, which he gave little heed to. To make matters worse, and to the great amusement of Morgoth, the Sons of Fëanor, seeking the Silmaril of Beren and Lúthien, had enacted two brutal Kinslayings that destroyed both Doriath and the Havens of Sirion. In this time of most dire need, the mariner Eärendil, by the guidance of a Silmaril which he wore in a circlet on his forehead, searched for and sailed to Valinor on behalf of the Free Peoples. There, he begged the Valar to pardon and aid the overmatched peoples of Middle-earth.

Despite having pledged to leave the Ñoldor to reap the bitter harvest of their folly in pursuing Morgoth, Manwë was moved to pity by Eärendil's plea and at last resolved to render aid. So it was that the Valar, along with many of the Maiar, the Vanyar, and the remaining Ñoldor in Valinor, came to Middle-earth in the mightiest gathering of arms in the history of Arda. The forces of the Edain joined the Host of the Valar as soon as it landed in Middle-earth, along with the remaining Ñoldor and Sindar of Middle-earth and "uncountable Dwarves from the lines of all seven Fathers". Though Manwë, as King of the Valar, held supreme authority, the host was commanded in the field by the Maia Eönwë, the herald and banner-bearer of Manwë.

The Valar themselves abstained from direct involvement in the war itself out of concern that the use of their immense, divine power on the field of battle would cause irreparable, catastrophic damage to Middle-earth and so instead participated from afar; organizing, blessing and directing their divine emissaries and allied armies. The Maiar who came took a more mixed role; some like Eönwë fought alongside the Children of Ilúvatar throughout the conflict while others, similar to the Valar, feared that the use of their power in battle would cause too much collateral damage and acted in more supportive and restorative capacities.
